name: RALPH Loop — Autonomous Codebase Improvement
description: PM-led multi-agent convergence loop. Reads the gate backlog, dispatches SWE/red-team/blue-team agents through gate stages, commits improvements, writes findings to the knowledge graph. Each workflow run is one RALPH iteration. Inspired by Benjamin Abt's RALPH method and thirdlayer's AutoAgent.

steps.name: 🚀 Bootstrap & Scope Check
steps.description:
Load skills, sync gate, and establish scope for this iteration.

1. Load `maenifold` and `gate` skills
2. Sync gate cache: `gate sync --root . --rebuild`
3. Check scope environment variables (`RALPH_TARGET_CRATE`, `RALPH_TARGET_PATH`)
4. Read `ralph/state/learnings.md` for known failure patterns
5. Read `AGENTS.md` for constitutional rules and RACI

State your scope before proceeding. If unscoped, state 'unscoped — selecting freely.'

SearchMemories.reason: Find prior RALPH iteration results and learnings

RecentActivity.reason: See what was done in recent iterations

next_actions: Select a task from the gate backlog

steps.name: 🎯 Task Selection
steps.description:
SEQUENTIAL THINKING REQUIRED

Select the next task to work on from the gate backlog.

1. Run `gate status --root .` to see pending tasks
2. Read each candidate task file in `todo/` for acceptance criteria
3. Check `done/` for ID conflicts before creating new tasks
4. **Epic handling:** If a task has `type: epic` in frontmatter, your job is to DECOMPOSE it into sub-tasks, not implement it. Create sub-task files. This IS a valid iteration.
5. Select ONE task that fits within change-size limits (≤12 files, ≤600 LOC)
6. If no viable tasks exist, consider creating improvement tasks from dogfooding observations

Use sequential thinking to reason through the selection — consider scope constraints, task difficulty, and dependency ordering.

SequentialThinking.reason: Reason through task selection considering scope, difficulty, and dependencies

SearchMemories.reason: Check knowledge graph for related prior work on the selected task

BuildContext.reason: Traverse concept neighbors for relevant context

stop_conditions: One task selected with ID and title stated
Task file read and acceptance criteria understood
Scope confirmed as within change-size limits

steps.name: 🛠️ SWE Dispatch
steps.description:
Dispatch a SWE agent to implement the selected task.

Use the Task tool to launch a `swe` agent with:
- Task ID and full acceptance criteria from the task file
- Scope constraints (crate/path)
- Build command: `cargo build --release -p <crate>` or `cd apps/desktop && npx vue-tsc --noEmit`
- Test command: `cargo test -p <crate>` or `cd apps/desktop && npm run build`
- `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/agents/<task-id>` for build isolation
- Model: per RACI table (default: `gpt-5.3-codex`)

Do NOT write code yourself. Do NOT troubleshoot SWE failures — if the SWE fails 3 times, fail the task via gate and move on.

After SWE completes, verify:
1. `git diff --stat` confirms files were modified
2. Modified files match the spec's file list
3. Spot-check at least one acceptance criterion against actual code

Task.reason: Dispatch SWE agent with complete context

next_actions: Record gate pass for SWE stage, proceed to red-team (if SDD/SLC) or blue-team (if lightweight)

swe_failure.condition: SWE fails after 3 attempts — gate fail the task, record learnings, skip to record-and-commit

steps.name: ✅ Gate SWE Pass
steps.description:
Record the SWE stage pass via gate.

`gate pass <task-id> --root . --agent swe --notes '<what was implemented>'`

If the task pipeline is `lightweight`, this advances to blue-team. If `sdd` or `slc`, this advances to red-team.

Check the task's pipeline to determine next step.

stop_conditions: Task state advanced to next stage
next_actions: If red-team stage: dispatch red-team agent
If blue-team stage: dispatch blue-team agent

steps.name: 🔴 Red-Team Dispatch (SDD/SLC only)
steps.description:
Dispatch a red-team agent to adversarially audit the SWE's changes.

Skip this step if the task pipeline is `lightweight` (no red-team stage).

Use the Task tool to launch a `red-team` agent with:
- The task spec and acceptance criteria
- `git diff` of the SWE's changes
- Model: `goldeneye` (per RACI)
- Instruction: audit ONLY files modified by the SWE, verdict on the delta

If red-team finds blocking issues:
1. `gate fail <task-id> --root . --agent red-team --notes '<findings>'`
2. Re-dispatch SWE with the findings (remediation cycle)
3. Max 2 remediation cycles, then escalate

If red-team passes:
1. `gate pass <task-id> --root . --agent red-team --notes '<verdict>'`

Task.reason: Dispatch red-team agent for adversarial audit

stop_conditions: If fail: remediation dispatched or escalated
next_actions: If fail: remediation cycle or skip to learnings

steps.name: 🔵 Blue-Team Dispatch
steps.description:
Dispatch a blue-team agent to verify build, tests, and acceptance criteria.

Use the Task tool to launch a `blue-team` agent with:
- The task spec and acceptance criteria
- Specific test commands to run
- Model: `claude-opus-4.5` (per RACI)
- Instruction: run ONLY tests for changed code, verify build, check LOC compliance

If blue-team fails:
1. `gate fail <task-id> --root . --agent blue-team --notes '<findings>'`
2. Re-dispatch SWE for fixes (remediation)

If blue-team passes:
1. `gate pass <task-id> --root . --agent blue-team --notes '<verdict>'`
2. This is the terminal stage — gate moves the task file to `done/`

stop_conditions: If terminal pass: task file moved to done/
next_actions: If pass: proceed to commit and record
If fail: remediation or skip to learnings

steps.name: 📝 Commit & Record to Knowledge Graph
steps.description:
SEQUENTIAL THINKING REQUIRED

Commit the completed work and record findings to the knowledge graph.

1. **Commit:**
   ```bash
   git add -A
   git commit -m '<description of change>

   Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>'
   ```

2. **Write memory note** to `mae-auto/iterations/` documenting:
   - What changed and why
   - Files modified with line counts
   - Gate task ID and pipeline used
   - Thinking session ID (if any)
   - Include `[[WikiLinks]]` to relevant domain concepts

3. **Update learnings** — append any new patterns to `ralph/state/learnings.md`:
   - What worked well
   - What failed and why
   - Operational patterns discovered

SequentialThinking.reason: Reflect on what worked and what to record for future iterations

WriteMemory.reason: Persist iteration results to knowledge graph

stop_conditions: Learnings updated if new patterns discovered

steps.name: 🏁 Convergence Check
steps.description:
Determine whether to continue or signal convergence.

1. Re-check `gate status --root .` for remaining pending tasks
2. If pending tasks remain within scope: DO NOT converge, the outer loop will run another iteration
3. If no viable pending tasks remain: `touch ralph/state/converged`
4. If the only remaining task is an epic: DO NOT converge — decompose it next iteration

**NEVER STOP voluntarily.** The outer shell loop controls iteration count. Your job is to signal convergence ONLY when the backlog is genuinely empty.

stop_conditions: Either: converged marker created, or: ready for next iteration
next_actions: Workflow complete — outer loop decides whether to run again
